patches.value: Let J=[r/2,3r/2] and take compact C from H003. M005 gives compact C×J. The continuous e_t is bounded there by K and vanishes outside C. C is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure. M008 gives integrability on C of the constant function K; M009 then gives integrability on ℝⁿ of b=K·1_C. For F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and F′(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ), every F(τ) is strongly measurable by continuity, F(r) integrable by N001, and F′(r) strongly measurable. Smoothness gives the pointwise derivative in τ, and |F′(τ)(x)|≤b(x) for τ∈J. M006 therefore applies and gives E differentiable at r with derivative ∫e_t(x,r)dx. This proves N002 for arbitrary r.

hypothesis_checks: C is measurable because compact subsets of Euclidean space are closed.
Lebesgue measure of compact C is finite.
K is a finite nonnegative real, so its extended norm is finite.
The constant K is integrable on C by M008.
C is measurable because it is compact in Euclidean space.
